words: oh hey. it was one of those dreams that feels too calm, like the air was holding its breath. the part that stays with me is my grandfather.
he’s just sitting across from me on this old train. not saying anything.
he was looking at me mostly, but it wasn't intense. more like he was waiting.
no hurry. like he had already decided whatever was next could take its time.
there was a brown leather suitcase on his knees. he kept both hands on it.
old-looking, worn at the corners. not sure about heavy. he didn't struggle with it or anything.
yeah he opened it. just lifted the lid and turned it so i could see inside.
letters. so many letters, all of them addressed to me.
i just looked. it didn't feel like i was supposed to take them yet.
the train stopped. right in the middle of nowhere, all snowy. we both got off.
quiet. really quiet. like the snow ate every sound. and cold, but not in a painful way.
everything was white and blue. like evening or early night, but you could still see fine.
we walked. through deep snow, toward this red door standing on its own. no house, no wall. just a door in its frame.
we both moved toward it, like there was no question. side by side, not really rushing.
he gave me the suitcase. not with words. just held it out. then nodded at the door.
i looked at the door. i think i already knew he wanted me to open it.
hard to say. it was bright, but it didn't feel jarring against all that snow. like it belonged there, even though it shouldn't.
yeah. i opened it and there was warm yellow light on the other side. then i woke up.
you got it right. only thing is he didn't just hand it over suddenly, it was more like he was passing it to me, and the nod came with it.
yeah exactly, gentle. like something being finally returned.
yeah, i'd like that
charcoal on blue-grey paper, i think. that blue of evening is right.
that sounds right. the worn seats especially. go with it.
however you imagine me is fine
oh wow, seven of them. i'll look now.
that middle one with him holding the suitcase open, that looks right to me.
yeah, exactly. that quiet is the whole dream.
the red door drawing feels a bit too bright to me. in the dream it was red, but the snow kind of dulled it.
yeah, that's exactly it. soft and a little muted. please.
perfect. that's much closer.
i think the whole set sits okay. the snow one with us walking, i can almost hear it.
it's strange, seeing it like this. but good strange.
take your time. i'm fine sitting with these for a bit.
the one of me opening the door with the yellow light, that's up now. it got the light right.
okay. no rush.
the letters one is up. seeing them all in there, it's a lot. but right.
yeah, the letters look right. packed in there, all paper and edges. no gaps.
the train exterior one just came up. it works.
it does. the nod isn't a huge gesture in the drawing, and that's right. it was small.
all seven are up now. i'm just looking at them.
it feels like the dream. nothing missing that i can tell. maybe just the quiet between them, but that's not something you can draw.

style.name: charcoal on blue-grey paper
style.line: drawn with smudged, soft strokes where the paper's tone becomes the blue of evening.
tokens: soft charcoal lines with variable pressure
style.lighting_rules: Light is faint, as if from a just-set sun, leaving shapes in twilight blues and greys. Edges soften into shadow, and no line is completely sharp. The surface seems to absorb light rather than reflect it.
